skill.name: image-to-video
skill.description: Guide for converting still images into short videos with the inference.sh belt CLI. Covers model selection, motion prompts, camera movement, stitching, upscaling, audio, and quality issues.
skill.summary: Plan controlled image-to-video animations and run them through remote inference models.
skill.author: 101-skills

security_audit.summary: Seven static findings are confirmed because they direct npx or belt commands that install tooling or submit work to remote services. The other 21 matches are Markdown delimiters, identifiers, links, or unrelated prose, not command execution or reconnaissance. Semantic review also found that the declared Bash permission allows every belt subcommand.

remediation.issue: The allowed-tools rule grants access to every belt subcommand.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict permissions to the exact belt commands required by the documented workflow, and require confirmation for account or installation operations.

remediation.issue: The setup directs users to install a third-party skill through npx.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the dependency to a reviewed version or immutable reference and ask for explicit approval before installation.

remediation.issue: Image and video assets may be processed by remote inference services.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose remote processing, provider terms, retention, costs, and privacy implications before submitting user media.

content.user_title: Animate Still Images into Short Videos
content.value_statement: Still images need precise motion direction to avoid distorted video. This skill selects suitable models and builds controlled prompts for short image-to-video workflows.
actual_capabilities: Compares six image-to-video models by motion style, speed, resolution, and content type.
Structures prompts with camera movement, subject motion, atmosphere, mood, and pace.
Provides belt CLI examples for landscapes, portraits, products, fabric, architecture, and cinemagraphs.
Recommends clip durations and explains how to stitch shorter clips.
Outlines a pipeline for image generation, animation, upscaling, audio creation, and media merging.
Identifies common causes of warping, unstable motion, and low-quality output.
limitations: Requires the belt CLI, an inference.sh account, network access, and access to remote model providers.
Model identifiers, availability, pricing, limits, and output capabilities may change.
Does not provide a local video engine or an offline generation workflow.
Face fidelity, motion stability, resolution, and audio quality depend on the source image and selected model.

use_cases.title: Animate Social Media Artwork
use_cases.description: Turn campaign images into short clips with subtle camera and environmental motion.

use_cases.title: Create Product Motion Studies
use_cases.description: Select models for product or fabric movement and produce controlled showcase prompts.

use_cases.title: Build Short Video Pipelines
use_cases.description: Plan connected generation, animation, upscaling, sound, and merging steps for production assets.

prompt_templates.title: Animate One Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Animate [image description] for [duration]. Use one gentle subject motion and keep the camera static. Recommend a suitable model.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Model and Motion
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare suitable models for [image type]. Recommend one model, one camera movement, and two subtle subject motions for a [duration] clip.
prompt_templates.scenario: Model selection for a specific source image

prompt_templates.title: Design a Product Reveal
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an image-to-video plan for [product]. Include model choice, camera path, material motion, lighting changes, duration, and artifact prevention.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-Stage Video Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a workflow for [project]. Include source creation, multiple short animations, continuity, upscaling, audio, merging, privacy checks, and quality review.

output_examples.input: Animate a portrait with natural movement for four seconds.
output: Recommended model: Wan 2.5 i2v for subtle facial motion.
Camera: static framing with a very slow push forward.
Motion: natural blinking, slight breathing, and gentle hair movement.
Quality note: avoid large head turns to reduce facial distortion.

output_examples.input: Create a short animation of a silk scarf product image.
output: Recommended model: Fabric 1.0 for cloth-focused motion.
Camera: slow orbit around the product.
Motion: soft rippling from one consistent breeze direction.
Duration: three to five seconds for stable material detail.

output_examples.input: Plan an eight-second landscape video with sound.
output_examples.output: Generate two short landscape clips with consistent camera direction, stitch them, create matching ambient audio, then merge and review continuity.

best_practices: Start with a high-resolution source and test a three-to-five-second clip before extending the sequence.
Use one primary camera movement and a small number of compatible subject motions.
Confirm provider costs, privacy terms, media rights, and retention rules before remote processing.
anti_patterns: Do not combine dramatic action, rapid camera motion, and multiple directions in one prompt.
Do not submit sensitive or unlicensed media without reviewing the remote provider terms.
Do not rely on a single long generation when several consistent short clips can preserve quality.

faq.question: Does this skill generate video by itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides model selection and belt CLI workflows that call remote inference services.

faq.question: Which model should I use for realistic motion?
faq.answer: The guide recommends Wan 2.5 i2v for realistic landscapes, portraits, and subtle natural movement.

faq.question: Can the workflow add audio?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes model-generated audio options and separate steps for creating and merging ambient sound.

faq.question: How long should each generated clip be?
faq.answer: Use three to five seconds for most work. Generate and stitch shorter clips when a longer sequence is required.

faq.question: Can this workflow run offline?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow requires the belt CLI, authentication, network access, and remote model services.

faq.question: Will portrait faces remain unchanged?
faq.answer: No model can guarantee exact identity preservation. Use subtle motion, short duration, and careful review for portraits.
